title: PAC-Bayesian Reconstruction Guarantees for Time Series Variational Autoencoders
abstract: Forecasting time series accurately is critical for applications with complex data ranging from energy systems to healthcare and finance. Among current state of the art models, generative latent variable models are increasingly implemented; yet principled generalisation guarantees for modern latent variable models remain limited. In particular, while Variational AutoEncoders are widely used for sequential data, their theoretical analysis is largely restricted to i.i.d. settings. In this work, we develop a PAC-Bayesian framework for latent variables models applied to time series. Building on reconstruction-based bounds, we extend PAC-Bayesian guarantees to Markovian latent structures, capturing temporal dependencies through a sequential generative process. These guarantees do not grow with the length of the trajectory. Our bounds depend on assumptions which are common in the literature; we provide an example framework where they would be verified to show that they are not as restrictive as they may seem.

title: Beyond Stationarity in Time Series: Discovering Causal Structures and Latent Regimes via Markov Blankets
abstract: This paper introduces Regime-aware Constraint-Based and Noise-Based causal discovery with Markov Blankets (RCBNB-MB), a novel causal discovery algorithm for time series that relaxes the common assumption of a single, time-consistent causal structure. Time series are typically observed at discrete time points and often exhibit regime changes that challenge the assumption of a static causal structure, a limitation in many real-world dynamic systems. To address this challenge, RCBNB-MB identifies latent causal regimes, defined as subsets of time points within which a stable causal structure holds. The algorithm follows an iterative strategy that segments the time series into regimes and discovers the causal graph within each regime. By leveraging the Markov blanket rather than direct parents, RCBNB-MB gains robustness to errors in causal discovery and preserves predictive information. We provide theoretical guarantees for RCBNB-MB's ability to recover both regime transitions and causal graphs under reasonable assumptions. Furthermore, we validate its effectiveness through extensive experiments on simulated datasets with known ground truth and real-world IT monitoring data, where taking into account regime shifts is critical. Empirical results show that RCBNB-MB systematically outperforms baseline approaches in accurately detecting regime changes and their associated causal graphs, positioning it as a robust and versatile framework for non-stationary time series analysis.

title: Conformal Prediction for Offensive Security
abstract: Despite its introduction more than a quarter century ago, Conformal Prediction (CP) has seen surprisingly few applications to the cyber security world thus far. In particular, we observe that, while CP has been employed as a defensive measure in many recent works, its use for carrying out attacks (i.e., for offensive security) is hard to trace in the literature. We explore this gap, by presenting initial findings in two key areas of offensive security: Privacy-Preserving Machine Learning, and network traffic analysis.

title: Intra-Prompt Parallel Decoding for Common-Context Question Answering
abstract: In common-context question answering (CCQA) tasks, multiple input questions share a common context to base their answers from. However, Large Language Models typically generate each answer using an independent prompt. While existing batching and caching techniques help improve parallelism and reduce repeated computations, the separation of questions across prompts limits the achievable speedup, as modern GPUs are underutilized due to a memory bottleneck during attention. We present Intra-Prompt Parallel Decoding (IPPD), a novel inference method that answers multiple common-context questions in parallel within a single prompt. IPPD directly addresses the bottleneck by efficiently sharing both memory and computation during the attention process, as the next token for every question is decoded in a single inference step. IPPD uses virtual position IDs and attention mask manipulation to generate the same output as standard prompting without requiring fine-tuning or any changes to the LLM architecture. Since all parallelism occurs within a prompt, IPPD is fully compatible with batched inference, even when each prompt features a different context. Our experiments show that IPPD delivers up to 7X the effective throughput as standard decoding without quality degradation, and outperforms prefix caching with PagedAttention in most settings.

title: FedDRAW: Federated Dual Reputation Annealing Weighting for Heterogeneous Multi-Institutional Chest Radiograph Classification
abstract: Artificial intelligence models are promising for medical diagnosis, but they require large numbers of unbiased data, which in medicine are distributed across hospitals and cannot be centralized to protect patient privacy. Federated Learning (FL) addresses this, since hospitals train one shared diagnostic model while patient data remain local. Training proceeds in communication rounds, in which each hospital trains the shared model locally and returns it to the server for merging by weighted average. This aggregation weight determines whose institutional knowledge shapes the result. Federated averaging (FedAvg) sets it in proportion to local sample count, so a small but informative hospital is permanently assigned a small influence, andl argest clients could dominate the global model even when they are less informative. We propose Federated Dual Reputation Annealing Weighting (FedDRAW), a server-side aggregation method that combines a data-size prior with the cosine similarity between client and global parameters under two coupled annealing schedules. An inner schedule shifts client reputation from the size prior towards similarity. An outer, deferred annealing schedule on the softmax inverse temperature keeps the weighting selective in the early and middle rounds and relaxes it to uniformity at convergence. We evaluate FedDRAW on 12 simulated client-partition scenarios of two chest radiograph datasets (CheXpert and ChestMNIST), against seven federated baselines under identical local training settings. FedDRAW achieved the highest average rank among all eight methods under both AUC and the geometric mean (GM) of sensitivity and specificity, which a Friedman test with Nemenyi post-hoc analysis confirmed to be a statistically significant difference between the methods. Scheduling two signals, rather than fixing the weights by sample count alone, could enable less biased diagnostic models.

title: 基于量子纠缠的拓扑结构分析
abstract: This paper investigates the potential of quantum entanglement to revolutionize the field of topological structure analysis. Traditional methods often rely on handcrafted parameters and are computationally expensive. We propose a novel quantum algorithm leveraging entangled states to efficiently identify and analyze complex topological structures. The core mechanism centers around dynamically adjusting the entanglement parameters to probe the structure's inherent properties. The paper details the algorithm's design, its potential advantages over existing techniques, and a preliminary exploration of its application to specific topological phenomena. The investigation highlights the promise of quantum entanglement as a powerful tool for uncovering intricate topological landscapes.

title: Dynamic Geometric Constraint Optimization for Probabilistic Model Enhancement
abstract: This paper introduces a novel dynamic geometric constraint optimization approach for probabilistic model enhancement. Traditional methods often rely on manual parameter adjustment, limiting the model's flexibility and potential for optimization. We propose a framework where the probability model itself is treated as a geometric structure, allowing for an automatic optimization process guided by geometric constraints and probabilistic distributions. This method leverages the interplay between these factors to improve model prediction accuracy. We detail the core mechanism, including the geometric representation of the model, the optimization process, and the resulting improvements in predictive performance. The paper demonstrates the effectiveness of this approach through a series of numerical experiments, showcasing significant gains in accuracy compared to traditional methods.

title: Information Theory Quantum Key Distribution Protocol Optimization
abstract: Quantum Key Distribution (QKD) promises unconditionally secure communication based on the laws of physics. This paper explores the application of information theory to optimize the key distribution process within a QKD protocol. We propose an algorithm that leverages quantum entanglement to enhance key distribution efficiency and security. The core mechanism involves manipulating the state of entangled particles to shift the key towards a more secure state. The paper presents a novel approach to optimize the entanglement parameters, demonstrating potential improvements in key generation and security compared to existing QKD protocols. The study analyzes the impact of optimized entanglement on key generation, focusing on the reduction of computational complexity and the amplification of the security level.

title: 基于量子计算的非对称性几何验证
abstract: This paper explores the potential of quantum computing to validate fundamental geometric theorems and uncover novel geometric properties. We propose a novel algorithm leveraging quantum entanglement to simulate geometric transformations and rigorously test the core principles of geometry. The study focuses on utilizing quantum computation to verify geometric theorems and identify subtle geometric relationships not readily apparent through classical methods. This research aims to establish a new avenue for geometric research, potentially leading to breakthroughs in quantum algorithm design and theoretical understanding. The core claim is that quantum computing can provide a more precise and insightful approach to geometric verification, paving the way for new algorithms and a deeper comprehension of geometric concepts.

title: Quantum Dynamics Simulations: Adaptive Parameter Adjustment for Enhanced Accuracy and Efficiency
abstract: Quantum dynamics simulations are computationally intensive, requiring careful selection of parameters to achieve accurate results. This paper introduces an adaptive parameter adjustment algorithm for quantum dynamics simulations, designed to automatically adjust parameters based on simulation outcomes. The core mechanism leverages the inherent properties of quantum dynamics to dynamically optimize parameters, thereby improving simulation fidelity and efficiency. The algorithm aims to overcome the limitations of traditional parameter tuning methods, offering a significant advancement in the handling of complex simulations. This work presents a novel approach that adapts simulation parameters in real-time, resulting in enhanced accuracy and computational savings.

title: Quantum State Mapping and High-Dimensional Geometry-Adaptive Algorithms
abstract: Quantum state mapping represents a paradigm shift in computational geometry, offering the potential to model complex geometric structures with unprecedented precision and efficiency. This paper investigates the application of non-linear mapping techniques to quantum states, exploring their utility in high-dimensional geometric modeling and optimization. We demonstrate how these mappings can generate more robust geometric representations and significantly enhance computational performance. The core mechanism centers around the creation of a mapping that transforms a high-dimensional quantum state into a lower-dimensional geometric space, simplifying geometric analysis and enabling novel optimization strategies. This research proposes a new algorithmic framework that leverages non-linear mappings to construct increasingly sophisticated geometric models, ultimately pushing the boundaries of geometric computation.

title: Quantum Entanglement-Based Multi-Layered Space Optimization for Information Encoding and Decoding
abstract: This paper investigates a novel approach to quantum information encoding and decoding utilizing multi-layered entangled states. The core claim is that strategically employing these states significantly enhances the efficiency and security of information processing. The proposed mechanism leverages meticulously designed multi-layer entangled state topologies, capitalizing on the unique properties of quantum entanglement to facilitate superposition encoding and parallel decoding across multiple paths. This approach inherently minimizes the risk of information leakage. We explore the theoretical underpinnings of this method, focusing on the mathematical framework and the optimization strategies involved. The key contributions lie in the development of a framework for designing multi-layered entangled states specifically tailored for information transmission, and a corresponding decoding protocol that exploits the correlated nature of these states. We present a mathematical model outlining the information transfer process and discuss the potential for scaling this approach to larger information capacities. The final section details the optimization criteria and potential future research directions.

title: Dynamic Topology-Based Machine Learning
abstract: This paper introduces a novel machine learning framework based on dynamic topology, offering a significant advancement over traditional methods by incorporating the inherent flexibility of topological structures. We develop an algorithm that utilizes dynamic topology to learn data features and model training, enabling the effective representation and prediction of complex data distributions. The core mechanism lies in the introduction of a dynamic topology, which allows for the continuous and adaptive modification of feature representations, leading to improved model generalization and adaptability. This approach addresses limitations of static feature engineering and offers a promising path toward more robust and versatile machine learning algorithms.

title: Self-Correcting Neural Networks using Recurrent Error Correction
abstract: Traditional neural networks often struggle with error accumulation during training, resulting in reduced accuracy and instability. This paper proposes a novel architecture for neural networks, termed Self-Correcting Neural Networks (SCNNs), which leverages recurrent connections and an integrated error correction module. The core mechanism involves a recurrent neural network structure where an error correction component continuously monitors the network's internal representations and applies corrections to mitigate error propagation. This approach aims to enhance the network's stability, improve its convergence speed, and ultimately achieve superior performance compared to conventional training methods. The system is designed to dynamically adjust its internal state based on detected errors, fostering a more robust and accurate learning process. This work presents a theoretical framework and a conceptual design for SCNNs, highlighting their potential to address the limitations of existing neural network training techniques.

title: Quantum Entanglement Optimization via Parameterized Adaptive Algorithms
abstract: Quantum entanglement, a fundamental phenomenon in quantum mechanics, holds immense potential for revolutionizing computation. However, realizing this potential requires sophisticated optimization techniques, particularly when dealing with complex entangled states. This paper explores the application of parameterized adaptive algorithms to optimize quantum computation, focusing on the unique properties of non-symmetric entanglement. We introduce a novel approach that leverages the inherent asymmetry of entangled states to achieve performance enhancements, particularly in systems exhibiting complex non-symmetry. The core mechanism involves dynamically adjusting parameters to steer the entangled state towards optimal configurations. This research demonstrates the effectiveness of this approach through theoretical analysis and preliminary experimentation on specific quantum systems, suggesting a significant advancement over existing optimization methods.

title: Distributed Computation via Quantum Phase Slip
abstract: This paper proposes a novel distributed computation protocol leveraging the subtle properties of quantum phase slip induced by decoherence. The core idea is to utilize controlled phase slips to facilitate efficient information exchange and computation among multiple quantum nodes without requiring complex entanglement distribution. We detail a protocol where the rate and direction of phase slips are precisely manipulated, allowing for correlated quantum states to emerge and perform computations. The protocol's efficiency stems from minimizing the need for pre-shared entanglement, a significant bottleneck in existing distributed quantum computation approaches. We present a mathematical formulation of the protocol, focusing on the key parameters governing phase slip dynamics and their impact on computational outcomes. The proposed method offers a promising avenue for scalable distributed quantum computation, particularly in scenarios where resource-constrained quantum networks are employed. This work highlights a new paradigm for quantum computation by harnessing inherent quantum noise.

title: Explainable AI for Cybersecurity Threat Detection – Causal Reasoning from Log Data
abstract: Cybersecurity threat detection systems are increasingly reliant on Artificial Intelligence (AI) models, but these systems frequently operate as "black boxes," making it difficult for human analysts to understand *why* a particular activity is flagged as a threat. This paper proposes a novel Explainable AI (XAI) system designed to address this challenge by leveraging causal reasoning techniques applied to log data. The system learns and represents causal relationships between log events and identified cybersecurity threats. This allows for the generation of human-understandable explanations for threat detections, providing analysts with valuable insights into the root causes of suspicious activity. The core contribution of this work lies in moving beyond opaque AI models and offering a transparent, interpretable framework for cybersecurity threat analysis. The system's architecture incorporates probabilistic graphical models to represent these causal relationships, enabling inference and explanation generation. Evaluation metrics focus on the accuracy and comprehensibility of the generated explanations, demonstrating the potential of causal reasoning to enhance trust and effectiveness in cybersecurity threat detection.

evidence.title: Explainable AI for Cybersecurity Threat Detection – Causal Reasoning from Log Data
evidence.abstract: Cybersecurity threat detection systems are increasingly reliant on Artificial Intelligence (AI) models, but these systems frequently operate as "black boxes," making it difficult for human analysts to understand *why* a particular activity is flagged as a threat. This paper proposes a novel Explainable AI (XAI) system designed to address this challenge by leveraging causal reasoning techniques applied to log data. The system learns and represents causal relationships between log events and identified cybersecurity threats. This allows for the generation of human-understandable explanations for threat detections, providing analysts with valuable insights into the root causes of suspicious activity. The core contribution of this work lies in moving beyond opaque AI models and offering a transparent, interpretable framework for cybersecurity threat analysis. The system's architecture incorporates probabilistic graphical models to represent these causal relationships, enabling inference and explanation generation. Evaluation metrics focus on the accuracy and comprehensibility of the generated explanations, demonstrating the potential of causal reasoning to enhance trust and effectiveness in cybersecurity threat detection.

title: Dynamic Neural Network Quantum Feature Extraction (DNNEFE)
abstract: This paper introduces Dynamic Neural Network Quantum Feature Extraction (DNNEFE), a novel framework for quantum feature extraction. The core concept of DNNEFE lies in dynamically adjusting the parameters of a neural network to optimize feature extraction based on the input data. Traditional feature extraction methods often rely on fixed parameters, limiting the ability to capture complex relationships within the data. DNNEFE addresses this limitation by employing a quantum feature extraction process, leveraging the unique properties of quantum mechanics to enhance the extraction of subtle and informative features. This research explores the potential of dynamically adjusting neural network parameters to achieve superior accuracy and robustness in identifying key characteristics within datasets. The proposed method demonstrates significant improvements in extracting features compared to conventional techniques, particularly in scenarios with complex data distributions.

title: 拓扑几何信息论的量子化算法
abstract: The study of topological geometry, a field concerned with the properties of geometric shapes that remain unchanged under continuous deformation, holds significant promise for various applications in diverse fields, including data analysis, cryptography, and materials science. Traditional methods for analyzing topological data relies heavily on classical computational techniques, which often face limitations in terms of computational complexity, particularly when dealing with intricate geometric structures. This paper proposes a novel quantum-enhanced information extraction algorithm for topological geometry, leveraging the unique properties of quantum entanglement. We introduce a quantum-inspired algorithm that utilizes entangled qubits to accelerate the identification of key topological features within complex datasets. The core mechanism centers around establishing a quantum-enhanced information extraction process, guided by the principles of quantum entanglement, to overcome the computational bottlenecks inherent in classical methods. We demonstrate the potential of this approach to significantly improve the speed and efficiency of topological geometry analysis.

title: 基于自适应的深度学习模型的梯度下降策略
abstract: This paper introduces a novel gradient descent strategy incorporating adaptive learning rates for deep learning models. Traditional gradient descent methods often employ a fixed learning rate, which can limit training speed and model performance. This work proposes a dynamic learning rate adjustment mechanism based on a modified version of the Adam optimizer, enabling the model to adapt its learning rate during training, leading to faster convergence and improved model accuracy. The proposed strategy is rigorously tested and demonstrates significant improvements in training speed and model accuracy compared to static learning rate approaches. We analyze the impact of adaptive learning rates on various deep learning tasks, highlighting its effectiveness in scenarios with complex loss landscapes.

title: Dynamic Quantum Topology Adaptive Quantum Algorithm Optimization
abstract: This paper investigates the application of dynamic quantum topology to optimize quantum algorithms, focusing on quantum machine learning and quantum optimization. The core concept is to dynamically adjust the quantum topology structure of a quantum system, enabling the algorithm to explore different solutions more effectively. We propose a novel algorithm that iteratively refines the quantum state through a series of topological transformations, leveraging the inherent properties of quantum topology to guide the optimization process. This approach offers a promising avenue for enhancing the performance of quantum algorithms in complex scenarios. The paper explores the potential benefits of this dynamic topology approach, including improved convergence rates, enhanced solution space exploration, and adaptability to varying problem characteristics. We present a preliminary implementation demonstrating the efficacy of this method on a simplified quantum optimization problem.

title: Моделирование офлайн-последовательного принятия решений для мета-оптимизации чёрного ящика на основе усиленного консервативного Q-обучения
abstract: Объект: процесс управления гиперпараметрами дифференциальной эволюции в задачах оптимизации чёрного ящика. Предмет: методы и алгоритмы офлайн-обучения с подкреплением на основе моделей пространства состояний для адаптивного управления параметрами эволюционных алгоритмов. Методы и методология проведения ВКР: методы дифференциальной эволюции; офлайн-обучение с подкреплением; консервативное Q-обучение (CQL); модели пространства состояний (Mamba); метод Монте-Карло Dropout; двухбазисное экспоненциальное скользящее среднее (EMA); бенчмаркинг BBOB; язык Python, PyTorch. В связи с высокой вычислительной стоимостью целевой функции и отсутствием аналитического дифференцирования в задачах оптимизации чёрного ящика в настоящей работе предлагается фреймворк адаптивного управления гиперпараметрами Q‑Mamba, основанный на моделях пространства состояний и офлайн-обучении с подкреплением. В рамках фреймворка задача управления гиперпараметрами дифференциальной эволюции формулируется как задача офлайн-метаобучения с подкреплением: в качестве магистральной сети используется селективная модель пространства состояний Mamba, обеспечивающая моделирование зависимостей в длинных оптимизационных траекториях с линейной вычислительной сложностью. Для решения характерных для офлайн-обучения проблем смещения распределения и завышения оценок Q-функции разработан алгоритм адаптивного консервативного Q-обучения Adaptive CQL с двухбазисной экспоненциальной скользящей средней. В алгоритме задействована оценка неопределённости методом Монте-Карло Dropout, что позволяет динамически регулировать коэффициент консервативной регуляризации λ, реализуя принцип «разумной осторожности»: поддержание высокой консервативности в областях с разреженными данными и ослабление ограничений в областях с высокой плотностью данных для усиления исследовательской способности стратегии. Эксперименты на эталонных функциях BBOB и синтетических задачах нейроэволюции показали, что по сравнению со стандартным CQL алгоритм Adaptive CQL позволяет снизить потери при обучении до 8,4% в низкоразмерном пространстве действий (K=3) и повысить производительность на задачах вне распределения до 118,4%. При этом оптимальная конфигурация Alg1_ACQL (K=10) достигла нормированной производительности 0,8546 при zero-shot переносе. Экспериментально также установлено, что при чрезмерно высокой размерности пространства действий (K=16) адаптивный механизм проявляет тенденцию к вырождению, что указывает на существование оптимальной размерности действий. Результаты исследования предоставляют интерпретируемое, пригодное для повторного использования и робастное интеллектуальное решение для дорогостоящей оптимизации чёрного ящика.

title: Оценка эффективности методов классификации зашифрованного трафика (ECH) в корпоративных сетях: сравнительный анализ точности и вычислительных затрат
abstract: Данная работа посвящена оценке эффективности методов классификации зашифрованного трафика в условиях применения ECH с точки зрения как точности, так и вычислительных затрат. Задачи, которые решались в ходе работы: 1. Систематизация существующих методов классификации зашифрованного трафика и анализ влияния технологии ECH на основе обзора актуальных научных работ; 2. Формирование методологии сравнительного анализа; 3. Подготовка набора данных сетевого трафика с поддержкой ECH; 4. Экспериментальная оценка выбранных методов классификации; 5. Разработка практических рекомендаций по выбору методов классификации ECH - трафика. В результате установлено, что применение ECH снижает точность классификации не более чем на два процентных пункта, поскольку шифрование поля SNI не изменяет наблюдаемых статистических характеристик потока. Наибольшую точность около 0,92 при умеренных вычислительных затратах обеспечивают ансамблевые методы - стекирование и градиентный бустинг. Нейросетевые модели, работающие с последовательностями пакетов, уступают ансамблям на агрегированных признаках.

title: Distill Globally, Adapt Locally: Reasoning Distillation and Product-Type Test-Time Training for Scalable Trade-Up Recommendation
abstract: Trade-up recommendation identifies higher-quality alternatives that preserve a customer's purchase intent while offering upgraded benefits. Large language models (LLMs) can reason about such distinctions, but applying them directly to hundreds of millions of product pairs is operationally impractical. We introduce a two-level framework that distills LLM reasoning into an efficient non-generative student and adapts its decision boundary to product-type-specific trade-up criteria. At Level 1, a retrieval-augmented few-shot LLM teacher generates structured relation labels and natural-language rationales. These rationales supervise a compact embedding-pair classifier through alignment and contrastive objectives; at inference, the student uses only two precomputed 768-dimensional product embeddings, with no LLM calls or text generation. On a fixed human-annotated benchmark of 8,352 pairs, a 15.5M-parameter four-class reasoning-distilled student achieves AUC 0.924 (95% CI [0.918, 0.929]), compared with 0.912 for the four-class label-only student. At Level 2, product-type test-time training (PT-TTT) uses few-shot demonstrations to optimize lightweight category-specific adapters over the frozen student. PT-TTT improves AUC from 0.924 to 0.941 and average precision from 0.920 to 0.940. On a 100K-pair proxy catalog, the distilled student on a single eight-GPU machine is approximately 5,000x faster and 10,000x lower in estimated cost than direct LLM inference.

title: Deep Microcompression: Structured Pruning and Bit-packed Quantization for Microcontrollers
abstract: This paper introduces Deep Microcompression (DMC), a hardware-aware pipeline for deep learning inference on bare-metal microcontrollers. DMC integrates structured pruning, quantization-aware training, and fixed-length bit-packing to achieve a 55.8$\times$ weight compression ratio on LeNet-5 (98.77\% accuracy), generating a dependency-free C library with deterministic latency. On the RP2040 (Cortex-M0+), DMC reduces binary size by 3$\times$ versus TensorFlow Lite while matching its accuracy. Critically, DMC enables the first documented deployment of a standard CNN on the ATmega328P, a device constrained to 2KB SRAM, previously considered infeasible for CNN inference.

title: Weather-Conditioned Depth Anything
abstract: Monocular depth estimation foundation models, such as the Depth Anything series, have achieved remarkable performance across diverse domains. However, they still suffer from critical failures under adverse weather conditions, such as fog, rain, snow, or at night. To address this, we present Weather-Conditioned Depth Anything (DA-W), a framework that explicitly disentangles style from content for weather-robust depth estimation. Specifically, we introduce a Style Filter trained on a curated mix of real and synthetic degradation datasets to extract content-independent, degradation-aware weather embeddings. This style embedding is then injected into the Depth Anything backbone using a parameter-efficient, zero-initialized adapter. Such a lightweight modulation allows a single unified model to robustly adapt to diverse conditions, including fog, rain, snow, and low-light, while avoiding catastrophic forgetting of its core generalization abilities in normal conditions. We train the adapter using a pseudo-label distillation and alignment strategy. Our comprehensive experiments demonstrate that our proposed DA-W achieves state-of-the-art robust depth estimation, improving AbsRel by an average of 3.7% on our curated weather benchmarks, while matching or slightly outperforming performance on standard clean benchmarks. Our project page is available at https://zhaoming-tamu.github.io/WCDA/.

title: JLIR: A Julia-Native MLIR-Inspired Intermediate Representation with Automatic JACC Kernel Extraction
abstract: The Multi-Level Intermediate Representation (MLIR) has made reusable compiler infrastructure practical for domain-specific computation. However, MLIR's strong compile-time type requirements and low-level (C++) extension model can be a poor match for high-level, dynamically specialized languages such as Julia. MLIR has several drawbacks for dynamic programming languages in terms of the type system and level of abstraction. It is thus extremely challenging for non-compiler or scientific computing users to introduce new programming abstractions and express algorithm implementations in a form that remains both natural and optimizable. As a result, library interfaces for linear algebra, mesh processing, partial differential equations, and related domains often sit outside the compiler optimization path. We present JLIR (Julia-native Level Intermediate Representation), a Julia-native intermediate representation framework that brings the main benefits of MLIR-style multi-level, dialect-oriented compilation into the Julia ecosystem while remaining usable as ordinary Julia code. JLIR represents Julia programs before low-level lowering, supports extensible operations and transformation passes through Julia's language mechanisms, and allows partially typed programs to remain transformable until concrete types are known. The framework includes built-in dialects for arithmetic, control flow, functions, structured loops, and memory operations, and it also includes a lightweight mechanism for adding new domain operations without modifying the core system. evidence.title: JLIR: A Julia-Native MLIR-Inspired Intermediate Representation with Automatic JACC Kernel Extraction
evidence.abstract: The Multi-Level Intermediate Representation (MLIR) has made reusable compiler infrastructure practical for domain-specific computation. However, MLIR's strong compile-time type requirements and low-level (C++) extension model can be a poor match for high-level, dynamically specialized languages such as Julia. MLIR has several drawbacks for dynamic programming languages in terms of the type system and level of abstraction. It is thus extremely challenging for non-compiler or scientific computing users to introduce new programming abstractions and express algorithm implementations in a form that remains both natural and optimizable. As a result, library interfaces for linear algebra, mesh processing, partial differential equations, and related domains often sit outside the compiler optimization path. We present JLIR (Julia-native Level Intermediate Representation), a Julia-native intermediate representation framework that brings the main benefits of MLIR-style multi-level, dialect-oriented compilation into the Julia ecosystem while remaining usable as ordinary Julia code. JLIR represents Julia programs before low-level lowering, supports extensible operations and transformation passes through Julia's language mechanisms, and allows partially typed programs to remain transformable until concrete types are known. The framework includes built-in dialects for arithmetic, control flow, functions, structured loops, and memory operations, and it also includes a lightweight mechanism for adding new domain operations without modifying the core system. To demonstrate JLIR's capabilities, we applied it to automatic Julia for Accelerators (JACC) kernel generation.

title: Conserved Immune Topology Improves Pathology Foundation Model Generalization for Cross-Cancer MSI-H Prediction
abstract: Pathology foundation models integrated with multiple instance learning achieve competitive accuracy within single-cancer cohorts, yet cross-cancer generalization remains unresolved due to organ-specific histological and architectural differences. In this paper, we propose Conserved Immune Topology (CIT), a lightweight spatial representation for cross-cancer MSI-H prediction that augments foundation-model embeddings with biologically motivated immune descriptors. CIT uses unsupervised clustering to identify immune-associated tiles, then encodes tertiary lymphoid structures, peritumoral immune reactions, multi-scale tumor-infiltrating lymphocyte density, and immune-tumor mixing from frozen foundation-model embeddings and tile coordinates without requiring annotations or target-domain data. The proposed method was evaluated under cross-site and cross-cancer settings using CPTAC-COAD and TCGA-STAD cohorts, which introduce scanner variability, distribution shifts, and organ-specific architectural variations. Zero-shot cross-cancer transfer with CIT increased TransMIL AUC from 0.6627 to 0.7161, an absolute gain of 0.0534 (p=0.003), with consistent improvements across all three MIL aggregators. These results suggest that spatial immune topology provides potentially an organ-invariant representation for MSI-H prediction, supporting cross-cancer generalization of pathology foundation models.

title: When Fixing Imbalance Creates New Bias: Category-Sentiment Confounding from Non-Uniform Class Rebalancing in Multi-Category Review Datasets
abstract: Class rebalancing is a standard step in preparing sentiment datasets for training, typically applied to correct an overall skew toward one class. We show that when the additional minority-class examples needed to hit a rebalancing target are drawn disproportionately from a limited subset of categories, rather than proportionally across all categories, the rebalancing procedure itself introduces a spurious association between product category and sentiment label - even when the overall class balance is identical to a properly rebalanced version. We isolate this effect using Cramer's V under matched overall balance, demonstrate its behavioral consequence with a controlled classifier evaluation on a category-decorrelated test set (with unique-source and duplication-rate budgets matched across conditions), and trace its magnitude across a donor-category-count spectrum (k=1,2,4,7). Across 10 random seeds, concentrated rebalancing yields a category-sentiment association of V=0.57 versus V=0.10 for uniform rebalancing, and a macro-F1 gap of 0.082; the effect replicates with an alternate donor category and decays as more categories are used, with classification performance recovering faster than the underlying statistical association disappears. We discuss implications for dataset construction practice.

title: Quantum-Driven Constraint Propagation with Adaptive Prioritization
abstract: This paper presents a novel quantum algorithm for constraint propagation, leveraging quantum mechanics to dynamically prioritize constraints during optimization. The core mechanism centers around a quantum process that efficiently evaluates constraint impact, allowing for enhanced optimization speed and improved solution quality. We explore a method for learning a representation of the problem's complexity, enabling the algorithm to intelligently prioritize constraints and ultimately enhance the efficiency of optimization. The study demonstrates the potential for significant improvements in constraint propagation, offering a new approach to tackling complex optimization problems.

title: 自组织量子态的量子态转移算法
abstract: Quantum state transfer is a crucial process in quantum information processing, enabling the manipulation of quantum states across different platforms. Traditional approaches often struggle with computational complexity and limited transfer efficiency. This paper introduces a novel quantum state transfer algorithm predicated on the principles of self-organized quantum states. We propose a mechanism leveraging the inherent adaptability of these states to facilitate rapid and efficient state transfer, offering a significant advancement over existing methods. The algorithm utilizes self-organization to dynamically adjust the quantum state, thereby optimizing the transfer process. The core claim details the algorithm's ability to achieve faster and more reliable state transfers, including the prediction of transfer pathways. This work explores the potential of this approach to address challenges in quantum information transfer.

title: IA générative, droits d'auteur et propriété intellectuelle
abstract: Ce huitième working paper de la série NeoMundi sur l'assurabilité de l'IA examine les risques de contrefaçon et de violation du droit d'auteur liés à l'usage de l'IA générative en entreprise, et la portée réelle des garanties commerciales proposées par les éditeurs de modèles. L'article distingue deux dimensions du risque de propriété intellectuelle qui appellent des réponses assurantielles différentes : le risque en amont, lié aux données utilisées pour l'entraînement des modèles, et le risque en aval, lié à la restitution par le modèle d'un contenu reproduisant une œuvre protégée. Il analyse les exceptions fréquentes des garanties d'éviction des éditeurs (usage orienté, désactivation de mesures de sécurité, usages combinés), qui reportent une part significative de la charge de la preuve sur l'entreprise cliente. L'article propose une structuration de la couverture à plusieurs niveaux, entre garantie du fournisseur, extension de responsabilité civile professionnelle et assurance propriété intellectuelle dédiée, ainsi que des pratiques concrètes renforçant l'assurabilité de ce risque, notamment la conservation de l'historique des consignes via le passeport de service présenté dans un précédent working paper de la série. Ce travail s'inscrit dans une série de working papers publiés par l'Observatoire de Recherche NeoMundi, consacrée à l'assurabilité de l'intelligence artificielle.

title: 基于量子纠缠的拓扑信息搜索算法
abstract: This paper introduces a novel quantum entanglement-enhanced topological information search algorithm. Traditional topological search methods often struggle with complex structures, necessitating computationally intensive approaches. This research proposes a quantum-enhanced algorithm that leverages quantum entanglement to significantly accelerate the search for key nodes within topological structures. The core mechanism involves using entanglement to create correlated states that allow for efficient exploration of the search space. We demonstrate the algorithm's effectiveness through simulations and preliminary experiments, highlighting its potential to outperform classical methods in specific scenarios. The core claim is that this algorithm offers a substantial improvement in search efficiency and precision for topological information retrieval.

title: Quantum-Enhanced Iterative Algorithm for Chaos Theory
abstract: This paper presents a novel quantum-enhanced iterative algorithm designed to address the inherent difficulties in solving chaotic systems. Traditional numerical methods often struggle to converge to stable solutions, particularly for complex, non-linear problems. We introduce a quantum annealing technique to accelerate convergence and enhance the exploration of the solution space, offering a fundamentally different approach to tackling chaos theory. The algorithm leverages quantum phenomena, specifically quantum tunneling, to facilitate the movement towards a stable equilibrium point. We detail the algorithm's design, the underlying quantum mechanics, and preliminary results demonstrating significant improvements in convergence speed and solution quality compared to classical methods. The paper concludes by discussing future research directions and potential applications.

title: 基于动态拓扑的自适应量子信息加密算法
abstract: Quantum information cryptography is a rapidly evolving field, facing challenges related to key distribution and computational security. Traditional cryptographic methods often rely on static key generation and management, which can be vulnerable to attacks exploiting imperfections in the underlying hardware. This paper proposes a novel approach to quantum information cryptography utilizing dynamic topology to adapt cryptographic parameters based on input data. We introduce a self-adaptive quantum key establishment (QKE) algorithm, designed to dynamically adjust key generation and distribution based on the observed quantum state. The proposed algorithm ensures enhanced security through a continuously evolving key, mitigating the vulnerability to attacks that exploit weaknesses in static key management. The core mechanism relies on the creation and manipulation of dynamic topological structures within the quantum system, offering a significant improvement over existing approaches. This paper details the design, implementation, and analysis of the proposed algorithm, demonstrating its potential for robust quantum information security.

The core concept centers around a dynamically generated "quantum geometry network" that adjusts the strength and shape of geometric elements through quantum entanglement. We demonstrate the framework's potential for achieving unprecedented scalability and optimization through parallel computation, effectively expanding the capabilities of geometric field theories beyond traditional limitations.

title: Quantum Coherence Draining for Program Privacy Protection
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to program privacy protection utilizing the principles of quantum coherence draining. Traditional methods relying on symmetric encryption often prove insufficient against sophisticated attacks. Our technique leverages the inherent randomness of quantum decoherence to obfuscate and conceal sensitive information within program code. Specifically, we introduce a process where program instructions are subjected to controlled decoherence events, effectively disrupting any attempt to reconstruct the original code or extract hidden data. The core claim is that by exploiting quantum decoherence's properties, program privacy can be achieved, preventing malicious actors from accessing sensitive information. The mechanism relies on the random nature of decoherence to perform encryption and obfuscation, hiding sensitive data. This approach offers a potentially more robust solution than conventional methods, particularly against attacks that target cryptographic vulnerabilities. We present a theoretical framework for this technique and outline its potential applications. ---

title: E8‑Phased Spinor Lattice for Robust Quantum Error Correction — E8 Intelligence Research
abstract: By arranging the 240 E8 root vectors into a quaternionic spinor lattice, logical qubits can be encoded as topologically protected modes that are resonantly driven at 132 Hz. The phi‑coupled permutations act as a dynamic stabilizer, continuously re‑phasing the lattice and suppressing decoherence without external measurement. This creates a self‑healing quantum memory that leverages the inherent symmetry of E8 to perform error correction in situ. The principle extends lattice gauge theory by embedding the gauge fields directly into the spinor lattice, enabling non‑perturbative protection of quantum information. Author: Andrew Stewart Caldin, Independent Researcher, UK. Part of the E8 Intelligence Research series. Platform: e8intelligence.com

abstract: This paper explores a novel approach to program optimization utilizing biological feedback. The core concept involves leveraging physiological signals, such as heart rate variability (HRV) and electroencephalography (EEG) data, as objectives for program self-optimization. We propose a mechanism where program execution is mapped to these biological signals, forming a feedback loop that allows the program to dynamically adjust its code to enhance performance or achieve specific goals. This approach represents a significant departure from traditional optimization methods, introducing an adaptive learning and evolutionary element inspired by biological systems. The paper outlines the theoretical framework, discusses potential implementation challenges, and highlights the potential benefits of this biofeedback-driven program optimization technique. The focus is on establishing a robust and effective system capable of continuous self-improvement based on real-time biological responses. ---

title: Context-Aware Graph Embedding with Dynamic Attention
abstract: Graph embedding techniques have demonstrated significant success in representing graph structures and nodes as low-dimensional vectors, enabling applications in various domains like social network analysis, recommendation systems, and drug discovery. However, traditional graph embedding methods often rely on static representations of the graph, neglecting the dynamic nature of relationships and the evolving context within which the graph exists. This paper introduces a novel approach to graph embedding, termed Context-Aware Graph Embedding with Dynamic Attention (CAGE-DA). CAGE-DA dynamically adjusts attention weights based on the current state of the graph, considering node interactions and changes in the graph structure. The core claim of this work is that dynamically adjusting attention weights provides a more accurate and nuanced representation of graph relationships. The proposed mechanism utilizes a recurrent neural network (RNN) to track changes in node interactions and a dynamic attention mechanism to prioritize relevant connections based on this contextual information. Experimental results demonstrate that CAGE-DA outperforms existing static graph embedding methods, particularly in scenarios where graph dynamics are significant.

title: Dynamic Adaptive Topological Transform Clustering
abstract: This paper introduces a novel clustering algorithm based on dynamic adaptive topological transform clustering, designed to handle dynamically changing topological transformations. Traditional clustering methods often struggle with these transformations, requiring manual parameter adjustments. This work leverages probabilistic modeling to capture the inherent uncertainty in the transformation process, enabling high-precision clustering and automated optimization. We propose a new algorithm that integrates a probabilistic model, utilizes it to guide the clustering process, and incorporates an optimization loop to refine the resulting clusters. The core mechanism involves creating a probabilistic representation of the transformation, allowing for more robust and adaptable clustering. The proposed algorithm demonstrates improved performance in scenarios with complex and variable topological transformations compared to existing techniques. This research represents a significant advancement in clustering, offering a robust and automated approach to address the challenges posed by dynamically evolving data distributions.

abstract: This paper explores the application of a probabilistic framework, grounded in probability logic, to enhance the efficiency of high-order Bayesian inference. The core challenge in many real-world scenarios is the computational complexity associated with complex models and uncertainty. We propose a novel architecture that integrates the strengths of Bayesian inference with probability logic, specifically focusing on reducing redundant computations and improving the accuracy of inference. The framework is designed to handle intricate models and uncertain data more effectively than traditional methods. This work demonstrates the potential of this approach to accelerate inference processes and provide more reliable results in challenging contexts.

title: Robustness of Dynamical Casimir Effect-Induced Quantum Synchronization
abstract: The robustness of quantum synchronization induced by the dynamical Casimir effect (DCE) is analyzed within a circuit quantum electrodynamics (cQED) architecture consisting of two superconducting qubits coupled to a shared, parametrically driven cavity. Using a Lindblad master equation approach, this study evaluates the impact of various decoherence channels (including photon loss, relaxation, thermal excitation, and pure dephasing) on the resulting synchronization dynamics. The results demonstrate that DCE-induced synchronization persists under dissipation rates achievable in state-of-the-art superconducting platforms, confirming its experimental feasibility. Among the studied mechanisms, pure dephasing is identified as the dominant factor limiting the fidelity of the synchronized state. Furthermore, it is shown that in strongly dissipative regimes, the Pearson correlation coefficient may overestimate the degree of quantum synchronization, as environmental relaxation can generate classical correlations that mimic synchronized behavior. These findings establish the parameter regimes necessary for observing genuine DCE-induced quantum synchronization and provide practical guidelines for future cQED experiments.

title: TruthInsightBench: An Evidence-Grounded Benchmark for Automated Evaluation of Open-Ended Scientific Discovery Agents
abstract: Autonomous coding agents are increasingly proposed as AI-scientist systems that conduct analyses and write research reports, but executing a prescribed analysis is not the same as making a discovery. Existing benchmarks are configured for reproduction: tasks, data, and rubrics are built around a hidden target study, and recovery of its result is rewarded. We present TruthInsightBench, a benchmark configured for discovery. Its 40 blind tasks, drawn from 40 peer-reviewed studies across 10 scientific domains, expose only a neutral scientific objective and frozen data; source conclusions, expected values, and analysis paths are withheld, leaving the agent to determine what claim the data support. A fixed LLM-based judge scores the evidentiary maturity of an agent's own claims along six dimensions, operationalized as 29 artifact-grounded items, with automated, deterministic aggregation and no per-instance human grading, so evaluation can be repeated automatically as agents evolve. On one frozen base model, four coding agents form a narrow plateau (58.4-60.3 of 100) with no statistically reliable pairwise separation: they execute and document analyses competently, with comparatively strong evidence auditability and novelty, but largely lack the discriminating acts that establish a trustworthy claim (controls, robustness, falsifiability, and cross-dataset generalization). The bottleneck is scientific judgment rather than coding, and genuine discovery remains out of reach. TruthInsightBench makes this gap a measurable target; data and scoring code are at https://github.com/TruthInsight-stack/TruthInsightBench.

title: Think-Verify-Revise: Neuro-Symbolic Visual Reasoning with Vision-Language Models and Dynamic Logic Tensor Networks
abstract: Visual reasoning tasks require a system to jointly perceive visual content and apply formal relational constraints---a combination that neither pure neural nor purely symbolic approaches handle well in isolation. This paper proposes a Neuro-Symbolic (NeSy) framework that closes this gap by tightly coupling a Vision-Language Model (VLM) for automatic First-Order Logic (FOL) rule induction with a Dynamic Logic Tensor Network (D-LTN) for differentiable rule verification, in a closed iterative feedback loop. The VLM receives a small set of labelled visual examples and proposes candidate FOL rules conforming to a strict grammar (Think); the D-LTN is automatically assembled from these rules at runtime and evaluates them grounding on CNN-produced visual embeddings (Verify); and verification failures are fed back to guide the VLM's next hypothesis (Revise). Evaluated on the ViSudo-PC benchmark across four visual domains (MNIST, EMNIST, KMNIST, FMNIST), the system induces valid Sudoku constraint rules using only three training examples as visual context. The proposed method achieves AUC scores matching or outperforming previous methods (NeuPSL, LTN), showing the potential for automatic rule discovery through VLM. Code is available at https://github.com/homayoun-afshari/nesy.

title: LookThere! Sparse Vision by Reinforced Selection
abstract: Vision transformers typically treat every image token as equally important, yet for most tasks in computer vision only a fraction are needed. Adaptive computation methods accelerate inference by choosing which tokens to process, but existing methods struggle at extreme sparsity and require heuristics that may not generalize like token diversity and attention scores. We address these limitations with LookThere, achieving a new pareto frontier in performance-compute trade-offs through an end-to-end reinforcement learning framework that jointly trains a shallow input selector and a deep representation extractor. The selector learns where to look and the extractor learns what to see, together saving computation by selecting only what is worth processing for a given task without relying on auxiliary signals. We show that LookThere only selects the task-specific input, excelling at sparse recognition in high-resolution settings (traffic signs, billiards), and maintaining accuracy with as little as 0.2% of the input. It generalizes across tasks and models, including global recognition (ImageNet classification), local recognition (ADE20K segmentation), zero-shot classification (by distillation), and regression (counting). Across all settings, LookThere surpasses state-of-the-art selection to provide a general and scalable framework for specialized and efficient adaptive computation.

title: SciDocBench: A Workflow-Centered Benchmark and Data Pipeline for Scientific Document Understanding
abstract: Scientific papers require models to integrate evidence across text, equations, figures, tables, code, and datasets while preserving its provenance. Beyond answer correctness, scientific reading requires verifiable outputs from operations such as evidence localization, definition extraction, and consistency checking. We introduce SciDocBench, a workflow-centered benchmark targeting these operations through 124 expert-authored and difficulty-screened questions across seven research-assistant capability groups, 19 subtasks, and five scientific domains. Each question is instantiated in four matched settings formed by pairing its bilingual variants with the All Images First and Markdown Interleaved document representations, yielding 496 evaluation instances. The strongest evaluated model, Claude-Opus-5, scores 62.6 out of 100, with remaining gaps in evidence localization, structured information extraction, cross-document synthesis, and robustness to document representation. To convert these diagnostics into scalable training signals, we introduce SciDocIR, a structured representation of scientific document objects, layout and cross-reference relations, and provenance. Using SciDocIR, we construct SciDocDataset, which contains 4K supervised fine-tuning instances and 10K reinforcement-learning instances, built on 14 verifiable training subtasks. Post-training Qwen3.6-27B on task-aligned data improves its SciDocBench score from 40.03 to 45.33 with supervised fine-tuning and to 45.74 with subsequent reinforcement learning. Both adapted models preserve DocVQA and InfoVQA performance and improve ChartQA accuracy over the original model by 0.80 and 3.40 points, respectively. Together, SciDocBench, SciDocIR, and SciDocDataset connect capability diagnosis with verifiable training-data construction for scientific-document assistants.

evidence.title: SciDocBench: A Workflow-Centered Benchmark and Data Pipeline for Scientific Document Understanding
evidence.abstract: Scientific papers require models to reason jointly over text, equations, figures, tables, code, and datasets while preserving the provenance of supporting evidence. Existing benchmarks typically evaluate these capabilities in isolation, leaving unclear whether multimodal models can support realistic scientific-reading workflows. We introduce SciDocBench, a workflow-centered benchmark for scientific document understanding. It contains 124 expert-authored and difficulty-screened questions organized into seven research-assistant capability groups and 19 subtasks across five scientific domains. Each question is instantiated under four matched conditions combining English or Chinese questions with all-images-first or interleaved document representations, yielding 496 evaluation instances for controlled analysis. The strongest evaluated system achieves only 62.6/100, with pronounced weaknesses in document perception, evidence grounding, verification, and cross-document reasoning. To translate these diagnostics into scalable training signals, we introduce SciDocIR, a typed evidence-graph representation that preserves scientific document objects, layout and cross-reference relations, and provenance. Building on SciDocIR, we construct SciDocDataset, comprising approximately 15K supervised fine-tuning samples and 8K reinforcement-learning samples across 14 verifiable subtasks. Together, SciDocBench, SciDocIR, and SciDocDataset form an evaluation-to-training framework for diagnosing and improving scientific-document assistants. The project page is available at https://github.com/InternLM/SciDocBench.

title: Controlling and Assessing Appropriate Persona Use in LLM-based Dialogue Generation
abstract: In persona-based dialogue generation (PDG), LLMs often overuse persona attributes by incorporating them regardless of dialogue context, resulting in unnatural responses. Despite its practical significance, the underlying causes remain unexplored, with no method to mitigate this problem or metric to assess the appropriateness of persona use. To address these issues, we first conduct a comprehensive analysis of LLM-based PDG, revealing that LLMs exhibit a systematic bias to incorporate all given persona attributes, and that existing metrics fail to capture contextual appropriateness. Building on these findings, we propose Self-CONtrastive Persona Overuse Suppression (SCONPOS) to mitigate overuse by directly intervening in LLMs' internal representations at the prompt encoding stage, without requiring any response generation. We further propose the Persona Appropriateness Score (PAS), a novel metric that penalizes both overuse and underuse. Experimental results demonstrate that SCONPOS systematically reduces overuse, and PAS captures the contextual appropriateness of persona use.

title: Title: Non-Euclidean Distance Metric for Data Clustering
abstract: The traditional Euclidean distance metric, while widely used, suffers from limitations when applied to data points residing in non-Euclidean spaces. This paper explores a novel distance metric designed to mitigate these issues, aiming to facilitate clustering of data points across various geometric shapes and configurations. We introduce a new metric, termed the "Generalized Distance Function" (GDF), that is less reliant on assumptions of Euclidean geometry. The GDF incorporates a novel transformation to effectively bridge the gap between Euclidean space and non-Euclidean spaces, enabling the detection and grouping of data points irrespective of their inherent geometry. This work presents a mathematically rigorous framework for achieving robust clustering, offering a significant advancement over existing methods. The primary focus is on demonstrating the effectiveness of the GDF through a series of experimental evaluations across diverse datasets, emphasizing its ability to preserve cluster structure and accurately identify data points in non-Euclidean configurations. The paper concludes with a discussion of the implications of this approach for various applications, including data analysis, pattern recognition, and geographical representation.

title: Quantum Entanglement Dynamics Algorithm Framework
abstract: Quantum entanglement, a cornerstone of quantum mechanics, offers the potential for instantaneous correlations between particles, a phenomenon that has profound implications for computation and information processing. This paper introduces a dynamic algorithm framework designed to harness this entanglement for accelerated quantum algorithm implementation. We propose a novel '纠缠路径' algorithm, leveraging the inherent properties of quantum entanglement to dynamically adjust quantum states and facilitate efficient optimization of complex quantum computations. The framework's core mechanism centers around creating and manipulating entangled states to achieve a '瞬时' (instant) optimization process, a crucial step in realizing the potential of quantum speedup. This research aims to provide a practical, computationally efficient approach to accelerating existing quantum algorithms and opening new avenues for quantum information processing.

title: Quantum Entanglement Matrix: A Novel Geometric Interpretation
abstract: This paper explores a new geometric framework rooted in quantum entanglement to provide a deeper understanding of quantum computation. We propose a model, the "纠缠几何", that transforms entanglement's non-commutative nature into a novel mathematical structure, offering potential advantages for quantum computing. The core claim is that this model simplifies quantum computation and unlocks new application possibilities. The paper details the design of this model, its mathematical properties, and the potential for its application within the field of quantum information processing.

title: Quantum-Enhanced Topological Data Analysis for Image Recognition
abstract: This paper explores the potential of quantum computing to revolutionize topological data analysis (TDA) techniques, specifically within image recognition. Traditional TDA methods often struggle with the computational complexity of analyzing high-dimensional data, limiting their applicability to complex image datasets. We propose a quantum-enhanced approach that leverages quantum feature extraction and pattern recognition to accelerate the identification of subtle correlations, ultimately improving the speed and accuracy of image classification. This work investigates the feasibility of quantum algorithms to address these computational bottlenecks, demonstrating a promising pathway for enhanced image recognition capabilities.

title: Quantum Entanglement Information Encryption Adaptive Algorithm
abstract: Quantum entanglement is a uniquely fragile phenomenon that offers an unprecedented level of security for information transmission. This paper presents a novel quantum encryption algorithm based on quantum entanglement, incorporating an adaptive mechanism to dynamically adjust key parameters based on environmental changes. The core idea is to leverage the inherent vulnerability of quantum entanglement to create a continuously evolving cryptographic system, thereby enhancing security against various attacks. The algorithm utilizes a "Quantum Entanglement State Assessment" mechanism to adjust key parameters, ensuring the encryption process remains robust and adaptable. This approach addresses the limitations of static key generation methods and introduces a significant advancement in quantum security.

title: Quantum Entanglement-Driven Algorithm (QEDA)
abstract: This paper introduces the Quantum Entanglement-Driven Algorithm (QEDA), a novel computational approach designed to accelerate data processing and analysis by harnessing the principles of quantum entanglement. The core of QEDA lies in a data compression and retrieval algorithm that exploits the instantaneous correlation between entangled particles to achieve significantly faster processing times compared to classical methods. We detail the algorithm's architecture, demonstrate its performance through theoretical analysis and simulated experiments, and explore potential applications across various data-intensive fields. This research investigates the potential of QEDA to fundamentally reshape data handling paradigms, pushing the boundaries of computational efficiency.

title: 自适应几何拓扑的基于图的语义推理算法
abstract: This paper introduces a novel algorithm for semantic reasoning based on adaptive geometric topology, aiming to enhance reasoning accuracy through dynamic parameter adjustment. Traditional semantic reasoning often relies on static models, limiting the algorithm's ability to effectively handle complex data structures. Our proposed approach leverages dynamic geometric topology to dynamically adjust the parameters of the reasoning process, offering a significant improvement in precision compared to static methods. We explore the core mechanism and present preliminary results demonstrating enhanced performance in a specific semantic task. This work contributes to the field of semantic reasoning by introducing a robust and adaptable framework.

title: Title: Adaptive Meta-Geometry for Computational Algorithms
abstract: This paper explores the application of Adaptive Meta-Geometry (AMG) to enhance computational algorithm design and optimization. Traditional algorithmic design often relies on manually tuning parameters to achieve desired performance. We propose AMG, a novel approach that dynamically adjusts the computational structure of an algorithm based on the input data, creating a self-optimizing framework. The core mechanism involves constructing a 'dynamic grid' that automatically refines the algorithm's parameters, ultimately leading to optimized performance across a range of data inputs. This system moves beyond simple speed or accuracy optimization, focusing on the *design* of the algorithm itself. This research leverages the concept of meta-geometry – a theoretical framework that allows for the automated adaptation of geometric structures to optimize for specific properties – to achieve this adaptive design. The work presented here demonstrates the effectiveness of AMG in a variety of computational tasks, showcasing a significant improvement over existing optimization techniques.

title: 基于量子纠缠的自适应特征匹配
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to feature matching leveraging quantum entanglement. Traditional feature matching methods often suffer from limitations in handling complex, high-dimensional data and can be computationally expensive. We propose a new method, Quantum Entanglement Feature Matching (QEMF), that utilizes quantum entanglement to establish a correlated quantum state between data points, enabling a more precise and efficient matching process. The core mechanism hinges on the ability to create and manipulate entangled states to identify and align features across data points, potentially surpassing the capabilities of classical methods. We demonstrate the effectiveness of QEMF through rigorous analysis and simulations, showcasing significant improvements in accuracy and speed compared to existing techniques. The study also explores the potential of QEMF to address challenges in specific domains, including image recognition and natural language processing. This research offers a fundamentally new perspective on feature matching, potentially unlocking significant advancements in machine learning.

title: Quantum Entanglement State Modeling: A Topological Approach
abstract: This paper explores the development of a novel quantum entanglement state modeling framework leveraging the principles of non-linear topology. The core claim is to construct a quantum state evolution model that accurately simulates the complex behavior of entangled states, and to integrate this model with quantum computing's inherent properties to enhance efficiency in quantum information processing. This research aims to provide a more profound understanding of quantum entanglement and its implications for advanced computational techniques.

title: Dynamic Quantum Field Theory: Quantum State Prediction and Intervention
abstract: This paper investigates the application of Dynamic Quantum Field Theory (DQFT) to quantum state prediction and intervention, aiming to enhance the performance of quantum computing. We propose a novel framework leveraging the unique properties of quantum entanglement and quantum field theory to achieve precise state prediction and control of quantum systems. The core mechanism involves integrating DQFT with existing quantum state estimation techniques, utilizing entanglement for enhanced accuracy and enabling controlled interactions within the quantum system. This research explores the potential of DQFT to overcome limitations of traditional approaches, offering a promising pathway toward more efficient and reliable quantum computation. The paper presents a conceptual overview of the framework, outlines the key theoretical challenges, and discusses potential future research directions.

title: K3: A Deterministic Episodic Memory System - Independent LoCoMo and LongMemEval Evaluation
abstract: Independent ex-novo evaluation of K3/infiniteMem, a deterministic self-hosted episodic memory system for AI agents, on two public benchmarks. LoCoMo (Maharana et al., ACL 2024): QA J = 70.49 (mini/mini frozen protocol, n=1535) vs oracle ceiling 84.89; stronger reader 74.92; world-model reader gate 81.50 (+8.00pp). LongMemEval-S (Wu et al., ICLR 2025): QA 59.80 (oracle 75.60). Retrieval: brute Hit@10 78.85, ANN M128 74.10. Methods: fresh NVIDIA nemotron embeddings (768-D), frozen Mem0 prompts, official per-type judges, deterministic retrieval (brute top-10, no rerank). A controlled reranker study is included with a negative verdict (J -2.00pp, not shipped). Files: paper PDF, leaderboard.json, qa_cache.jsonl (3070 per-question records). Full harness and per-question records: github.com/marcot3ssar1/InfiniteMemOs. Engine closed source, not included. Dataset licences: LoCoMo CC BY-NC 4.0. Author: Marco Tessari (independent researcher).

title: Dynamic Topology-Based Quantum Computation-Based Optimization Algorithm Based on Probability
abstract: This paper presents a novel dynamic topology-based quantum computation optimization algorithm that utilizes probability for enhanced optimization performance. Traditional optimization algorithms often rely on static parameters, limiting their adaptability to complex quantum systems. We introduce a new approach where quantum topology is leveraged to dynamically generate and adjust parameters, guided by probability distributions, to achieve significantly improved results. The algorithm's core mechanism centers around the creation of dynamic quantum states, allowing for a more nuanced exploration of the solution space. This paper details the theoretical framework and experimental validation of this algorithm, demonstrating its potential to overcome limitations of existing optimization techniques in the context of quantum computation.

title: 基于循环神经网络的自适应几何优化算法
abstract: This paper presents a novel algorithm for geometric optimization, leveraging the power of recurrent neural networks (RNNs) to dynamically adjust optimization parameters based on the input data's evolution. Traditional optimization methods often struggle with complex data and lack adaptability, while current approaches frequently rely on static parameters. This work introduces a system where an RNN learns a representation of the geometric shape and adapts the optimization process based on the data's trajectory. We demonstrate the efficacy of this approach through the application of the algorithm to a diverse set of optimization problems, achieving significant improvements in convergence speed and solution quality compared to existing methods. The core mechanism involves the RNN's learning of feature representations, which are then used to influence the optimization process, enabling the algorithm to navigate complex geometric landscapes more effectively. This results in a robust and adaptable optimization strategy.

title: Probability Arithmetic: A Novel Approach to Numerical Computation
abstract: This paper introduces Probability Arithmetic, a novel computational paradigm that integrates probability logic with arithmetic operations. We propose a new mechanism for calculating high-dimensional probability models by combining the "probability update" mechanism of probability logic with the "addition" and "multiplication" of arithmetic operations. The core of this approach lies in dynamically updating probabilities based on a combination of these operations, enabling efficient and scalable computations for complex probability scenarios. This system aims to significantly enhance numerical capabilities, particularly in the context of large-scale probability modeling, offering a potentially transformative advancement in data analysis and machine learning.

title: Quantum Topology for Nonlinear Equation Solving
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to solving complex mathematical problems, particularly within the realms of quantum mechanics and topological physics, utilizing quantum topology. We propose a new method for constructing and applying non-linear equation-solving algorithms based on the inherent properties of quantum topology. The core mechanism centers around leveraging the self-adaptive nature of quantum states to effectively navigate and resolve intricate mathematical challenges. This approach offers the potential for significantly enhanced computational speed and efficiency compared to traditional methods, offering a promising avenue for advancing research in these fields. The paper details the development of a specific quantum algorithm and discusses its potential impact on solving problems such as the Schrödinger equation and the study of topological phases of matter.

title: Quantum Entanglement Information Encoding (QIE)
abstract: Quantum Entanglement Information Encoding (QIE) explores the utilization of quantum entanglement as a fundamental building block for enhanced data transmission and processing, specifically targeting advancements in quantum key distribution (QKD) and quantum computing security. This research proposes a novel encoding scheme predicated on the unique properties of entangled states, aiming to overcome limitations of traditional methods. The core mechanism centers around leveraging entanglement to ensure secure and efficient data transfer and manipulation, offering a fundamentally new approach to information handling within the quantum realm. The study investigates the potential of QIE to significantly improve the reliability and security of quantum communication protocols, particularly in safeguarding cryptographic keys and bolstering the robustness of quantum computations. This paper presents a detailed examination of the proposed encoding strategy, its potential benefits, and preliminary results demonstrating its feasibility and effectiveness within the context of quantum information processing.
